assumptions.sensitivity: The paper names gls but not the criterion. Maximum likelihood does not converge for Model 1a on the breast data (nlme: false convergence; MRPL19's variance collapses towards 0), and for Model 2 it lowers the gene SDs by 6 to 16% (hypotheses.json).

items.label: Table 1, 95% confidence intervals

assumptions.what: Wald intervals on the log SDs from the numerical Hessian (Richardson extrapolation) of the REML likelihood
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper does not say how it computed the intervals. nlme's intervals() gives the same kind of interval from a coarser Hessian: across 24 equivalent parameterizations its bounds move by up to 0.013 (PSMC4's lower bound) and reach every printed bound.

cause.summary: The printed bounds are nlme's approximate intervals, whose numerical Hessian moves them in the third decimal with the order of the rows and the contrasts; across 24 such parameterizations nlme 3.1-164 reaches all 12 printed bounds. Ours, from an accurate Hessian, are within 0.002 of every printed bound.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The intervals are nlme's intervals(), which depend on the parameterization
hypotheses.test: intervals() for each gene as the varIdent reference, under treatment and sum contrasts and two row orders (24 fits)

hypotheses.hypothesis: The intervals come from maximum likelihood
hypotheses.test: Model 1a by ML

fields.name: p, microarray-selected genes against GAPD and ACTB

assumptions.what: The test: a likelihood ratio test of Model 1a against the model in which the four microarray-selected genes share one variance and GAPD and ACTB another (REML, 4 degrees of freedom)
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper does not name its test. This is the only one of four readings tried that gives 0.0014 (0.00139). The others: one variance for each group against one for all, p = 1.8e-9; a t test of the six SDs, p = 0.032; a t test of their logs, p = 0.049.

assumptions.what: Variance of the log geometric mean of a set: sum of sigma_j^2 over the set divided by |S|^2
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper prints the divisor |S|, which gives none of rows 2 to 6 (row 2: 0.2430 against 0.1718); |S|^2, the variance of a mean, gives rows 1 to 5 as printed and row 6 one unit off. See text.set_variance_formula.

cause.summary: Every set and five of the six SDs come back as printed; the six-gene SD is 0.151354, printed 0.1513, 0.000004 above the rounding boundary. Optimizer settings, the rounded SDs of Table 1 and truncation do not explain it.

hypotheses.hypothesis: An optimizer setting of the 2004 fit
hypotheses.test: 36 fits: each gene as the varIdent reference, two contrast codings, convergence tolerances 1e-6, 1e-4 and 1e-3

hypotheses.hypothesis: Computed from the rounded SDs of Table 1
hypotheses.test: The six printed SDs give 0.1514

hypotheses.hypothesis: Truncated instead of rounded
hypotheses.test: Truncation gives row 6 0.1513 but rows 1, 3 and 4 as 0.2181, 0.1493 and 0.1489 against the printed 0.2182, 0.1494 and 0.1490

items.label: Methods: the printed bounds on the M-value under Model 1

check.detail: under Model 1a's SDs (R = 2.38) the printed bounds sigma_j^2 sqrt(1 + 1/R^2) <= M_j <= sigma_j^2 sqrt(1 + R^2) fail; with sigma_j in place of sigma_j^2 they hold

cause.summary: The bounds print sigma_j^2 where sigma_j belongs (M is a mean of SDs): with sigma_j they hold for Model 1a's SDs, with sigma_j^2 they fail.

hypotheses.hypothesis: sigma_j^2 is a slip for sigma_j
hypotheses.test: Both forms against the M-values implied by Model 1a's SDs

items.label: Methods: the four candidate genes chosen from microarrays

cause.summary: A SAS selection of genes with 'a small range of expression' and 'the least variance' on 62 arrays (Perou et al. 2000 and cell lines), with no thresholds; it cannot be rerun as described, and its result (the four genes) is the paper's input, not one of its results.
